applies_why: The judge text is a ruling on a verse-level link collision, so K-C's chain-weighing requirement governs it.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse.' Reading 1: the judge must compare the whole pressed chain against the opposing chain by footing rather than splitting the dispute into separate wording and application points. Reading 2: the rule only bars expressly evaluating one verse at a time and permits an underdetermined finding when the parties' answers address different aspects.
why: The judge declared the Isaiah 7:14 collision underdetermined by separating the challenger's wording answer from the defender's application answer, rather than weighing the pressed chains together by footing as K-C requires.
